questions.stem: A 28-year-old man returns from a mountain camping trip with 8 days of nausea, cramping, and bloating. His stools smell terrible, he has excessive gas, and he feels plain tired. He recalls drinking untreated water from a stream. His abdomen is mildly tender and distended, with no rebound and no organomegaly. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

explanation.summary: Metronidazole is the drug of choice for giardiasis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ingesting untreated mountain stream water followed by bloating, foul-smelling stools, flatulence, and fatigue is the classic picture of Giardia, a parasite that beavers notoriously carry into such streams. Metronidazole is the drug of choice for giardiasis. It is absorbed in the intestinal tract and partially excreted in bile, so it acts both in tissue and in the intestinal lumen. With a history this straightforward, empiric treatment is reasonable, since stool testing delays therapy and adds cost without changing management.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Albendazole is a benzimidazole for helminths such as ascariasis, neurocysticercosis, and hookworm, not for protozoa.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Ivermectin is the drug of choice for strongyloidiasis and onchocerciasis, both helminth infections.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Praziquantel is used for schistosomiasis and intestinal tapeworms, which are helminth infections.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pyrimethamine is the agent commonly used for toxoplasmosis, a different protozoal infection.

questions.topicName: Agents treating Helminthic and Protozoal infections

questions.stem: In a laboratory model, metronidazole enters Trichomonas and anaerobic bacteria as an inactive compound and becomes cytotoxic only after an intracellular event. Which of the following is required to activate the drug inside the organism?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hydrolysis by esterases in the worm cuticle

choices.label: C
choices.text: Oxidation by host hepatic cytochrome P450

choices.label: D
choices.text: Phosphorylation by a parasite thymidine kinase

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reduction by ferredoxin and related electron transport proteins

explanation.summary: Metronidazole must be reduced intracellularly by electron transport proteins such as ferredoxin before it can kill.
explanation.whyCorrect: Metronidazole is active only when it is reduced intracellularly by electron transport proteins such as ferredoxin. The reduced drug and the free radicals it generates interfere with DNA synthesis and can result in DNA degradation. Only organisms that carry the necessary electron transport machinery, such as anaerobic bacteria and susceptible protozoa, perform this reduction, which is the basis of the drug's selectivity.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acetylation is not part of metronidazole activation; the brick describes reduction, not acetyl transfer.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Metronidazole is an antiprotozoal and antianaerobic agent and does not depend on worm cuticle enzymes.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Host P450 oxidation would occur in the liver, not inside the organism, and does not generate the active species.
whyWrongByChoice.D: No kinase step is involved; metronidazole is not a nucleoside analogue requiring phosphorylation.

questions.topicName: Agents treating Helminthic and Protozoal infections

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman is prescribed metronidazole for trichomoniasis. She asks whether she may drink wine at a wedding this weekend. Which of the following is she at risk for if she drinks alcohol?

explanation.summary: Alcohol combined with metronidazole can precipitate a disulfiram-like reaction.
explanation.whyCorrect: Metronidazole can cause a disulfiram-like reaction when combined with alcohol, producing flushing, tachycardia, and nausea. Alcohol should therefore be avoided during therapy and for 3 days after the last dose. This interaction is one of the counseling points that accompanies every prescription for the drug.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acute dystonic reactions are not described with metronidazole use.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hemolysis with jaundice is not a reaction attributed to metronidazole and alcohol.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Optic neuritis is not a reported consequence of combining metronidazole with alcohol.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A blistering photosensitivity rash is not among the described adverse effects of metronidazole.

questions.topicName: Agents treating Helminthic and Protozoal infections

questions.stem: The reaction that occurs when alcohol is taken with metronidazole is described as disulfiram-like. Disulfiram itself deters drinking by which of the following actions?

explanation.summary: Disulfiram inhibits acetaldehyde dehydrogenase, so acetaldehyde accumulates after a drink.
explanation.whyCorrect: Disulfiram was used in the past to treat alcohol dependence. It increases sensitivity to alcohol by inhibiting acetaldehyde dehydrogenase, so acetaldehyde accumulates and produces nausea, vomiting, and headache as a deterrent to drinking. Drugs said to cause a disulfiram-like reaction either inhibit this same enzyme or act in other ways to slow alcohol metabolism.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Activating aldehyde reductase would help clear the aldehyde rather than cause its buildup.
whyWrongByChoice.B: GABA-A blockade is not the mechanism by which disulfiram discourages drinking.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Inducing P450 would accelerate alcohol clearance and would not produce the deterrent symptoms.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Blocking alcohol dehydrogenase would reduce acetaldehyde formation rather than let it accumulate.

questions.stem: A 23-year-old woman at 8 weeks' gestation is diagnosed with trichomoniasis. Which of the following statements about metronidazole applies to her?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is contraindicated in the first trimester

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is contraindicated in the third trimester only

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is contraindicated only during breastfeeding

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is safe at any dose throughout pregnancy

choices.label: E
choices.text: It must be given intravenously during pregnancy

explanation.summary: Metronidazole is contraindicated in the first trimester of pregnancy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Metronidazole is generally well tolerated, but it is contraindicated in the first trimester of pregnancy. At 8 weeks' gestation this patient is still in the first trimester, so metronidazole should not be used and an alternative approach is required. The other standard cautions with the drug are headache, nausea, metallic taste, and the disulfiram-like reaction with alcohol.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The contraindication applies to the first trimester, not the third.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Breastfeeding is not the restriction described for this drug.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The drug is not considered safe at any point in pregnancy; the first trimester is an explicit contraindication.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Route of administration does not remove the first-trimester contraindication.

questions.topicName: Agents treating Helminthic and Protozoal infections

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man taking metronidazole for amebiasis complains of a persistent unpleasant taste in his mouth, along with headache and nausea. Which of the following is he most likely describing?

explanation.summary: Headache, nausea, and a metallic taste are the most common adverse effects of metronidazole.
explanation.whyCorrect: Metronidazole is generally well tolerated, and its most common adverse effects are headache, nausea, and metallic taste. This patient has all three. These effects are nuisance reactions rather than reasons to stop the drug in most cases.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Discolored urine is not among the common adverse effects attributed to metronidazole.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Gum overgrowth is not a listed adverse effect of this agent.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ototoxicity is not described as a reaction to metronidazole.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Scleral discoloration is not a reported metronidazole reaction.

questions.topicName: Agents treating Helminthic and Protozoal infections

questions.stem: A patient takes the final dose of her metronidazole course today and asks how much longer she must keep avoiding alcohol. Which of the following is the most appropriate answer?

explanation.summary: Alcohol should be avoided during metronidazole therapy and for 3 days after the last dose.
explanation.whyCorrect: Alcohol should be avoided during metronidazole use and for 3 days after the course is finished. Drinking within that window risks a disulfiram-like reaction with flushing, tachycardia, and nausea. Counseling patients on the specific 3-day interval is more useful than a vague instruction to avoid alcohol.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Resuming alcohol immediately leaves the patient exposed to the disulfiram-like reaction.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A month of abstinence is not required after metronidazole.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A 12-hour interval is shorter than the recommended wait.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Two weeks is longer than the interval described for this drug.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the way metronidazole crosses membranes to be absorbed after an oral dose?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Active uptake by an organic anion transporter

choices.label: B
choices.text: Facilitated diffusion through a nucleoside carrier

choices.label: D
choices.text: Passive diffusion in its unionized form

explanation.summary: Metronidazole is absorbed by passive diffusion in its unionized form.
explanation.whyCorrect: Metronidazole is absorbed by passive diffusion in its unionized form, which is why it distributes so widely and can reach tissues beyond the gut. Only after it is inside the organism and reduced by electron transport proteins does it become an active cytotoxic species. Good absorption plus intracellular activation is what gives the drug its broad usefulness.

whyWrongByChoice.A: No carrier-mediated active transport step is involved in metronidazole absorption.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Metronidazole is not a nucleoside and does not use a nucleoside carrier.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Absorption is transcellular by diffusion, not through tight junctions.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Endocytosis is not how this small, lipid-permeable molecule enters cells.

questions.topicName: Agents treating Helminthic and Protozoal infections

questions.stem: Metronidazole is effective against organisms that have invaded tissue and also against organisms that remain in the intestinal lumen. Which of the following properties best explains its luminal activity?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is concentrated in red cells and released into the gut

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is eliminated unchanged by glomerular filtration

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is not absorbed from the intestinal tract at all

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is partially excreted in bile and returns to the intestinal tract

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is secreted into saliva and continuously swallowed

explanation.summary: Biliary excretion returns metronidazole to the intestinal lumen, so it works in tissue and lumen alike.
explanation.whyCorrect: Metronidazole is mostly absorbed in the intestinal tract and is partially excreted through bile. Because bile carries drug back into the gut, the agent acts not only in the tissues but also in the intestinal lumen. This dual exposure is part of why it works well for luminal protozoa such as Giardia as well as for infection that has spread past the GI tract.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Erythrocyte sequestration is not a described feature of metronidazole disposition.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Renal elimination would not return drug to the intestinal lumen.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The drug is in fact mostly absorbed from the intestinal tract, not left unabsorbed.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Salivary secretion is not the route described for its luminal presence.

questions.topicName: Agents treating Helminthic and Protozoal infections

questions.stem: Metronidazole reliably kills anaerobic bacteria but has essentially no useful activity against strictly aerobic organisms. Which feature of anaerobes best explains this difference?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They carry efflux pumps that fail without oxygen

choices.label: B
choices.text: They concentrate the drug through aerobic glycolysis

choices.label: C
choices.text: They have a thicker outer membrane that traps the drug

choices.label: D
choices.text: They have the electron transport proteins that reduce the drug

choices.label: E
choices.text: They lack a cell wall and therefore take up more drug

explanation.summary: Anaerobic bacteria possess the electron transport needed to reduce metronidazole to its active form.
explanation.whyCorrect: Anaerobic bacteria have the electron transport necessary for reduction of metronidazole. The drug is reduced by these organisms, and the reduced metronidazole with its free radicals interferes with DNA synthesis and degrades DNA. Because the reducing machinery is what turns the drug on, organisms lacking it are spared, and this is why metronidazole provides coverage for anaerobic infections.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Efflux pump activity is not the mechanism described for this drug's selectivity.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Anaerobes do not rely on aerobic glycolysis, and drug concentration is not the explanation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Membrane thickness is not the basis of metronidazole selectivity.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Anaerobes are not defined by an absent cell wall, and wall status is not what activates the drug.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman with vaginal trichomoniasis had intolerable nausea the last time she took metronidazole. Which of the following agents has activity against amebiasis, giardiasis, and vaginal trichomoniasis and may be better tolerated?

explanation.summary: Tinidazole covers amebiasis, giardiasis, and vaginal trichomoniasis and may be better tolerated than metronidazole.
explanation.whyCorrect: Tinidazole has activity against amebiasis, giardiasis, and vaginal trichomoniasis, and it may be better tolerated than metronidazole. It shares the nitroimidazole mechanism of free-radical formation and inhibition of DNA synthesis, and it carries the same disulfiram reaction with alcohol. For a patient who could not tolerate metronidazole, it is the logical substitute for the same spectrum.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Mebendazole is a benzimidazole for helminth infections, not for protozoa.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Pentamidine is used for Trichomonas but does not cover amebiasis and giardiasis as described.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Praziquantel treats schistosomiasis and intestinal tapeworms, which are helminths.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Pyrimethamine is used for toxoplasmosis and does not cover this spectrum.

questions.topicName: Agents treating Helminthic and Protozoal infections

questions.stem: A 35-year-old man has trichomoniasis that has extended beyond the genitourinary tract into adjacent tissue. Which of the following agents is the drug of choice for both intestinal and extraintestinal trichomoniasis?

explanation.summary: Metronidazole is the drug of choice for giardiasis and for intestinal or extraintestinal trichomoniasis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Metronidazole can be used to treat infection that has spread past the GI tract to other parts of the body, and it is the drug of choice for giardiasis and for intestinal or extraintestinal trichomoniasis. Because it is well absorbed and also partially excreted in bile, it reaches both tissue sites and the intestinal lumen. That combination of distribution is what makes it useful when the infection is no longer confined to the gut.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Albendazole is a benzimidazole used for helminths such as ascariasis and neurocysticercosis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Ivermectin treats strongyloidiasis and onchocerciasis, not protozoal disease.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Praziquantel is reserved for schistosomiasis and intestinal tapeworms.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pyrimethamine is the antiprotozoal commonly used for toxoplasmosis, not trichomoniasis.
